directAnswer: Ray tracing may not work due to outdated drivers, insufficient hardware capabilities, or incorrect game settings.
summary: This guide addresses common reasons ray tracing may not function properly and offers troubleshooting steps.

sections.heading: Check Your Graphics Drivers
sections.body: Ensure that your graphics drivers are up to date. For NVIDIA, use GeForce Experience to check for updates. For AMD, use the Radeon Software.

sections.heading: Verify Hardware Compatibility
sections.body: Ray tracing requires specific GPU models, such as NVIDIA's RTX series or AMD's RX 6000 series. Confirm that your GPU supports ray tracing.

sections.heading: Adjust Game Settings
sections.body: In the game settings, ensure that ray tracing is enabled. The path may vary by game, but it is typically found under Graphics or Video settings.

steps.title: Update Graphics Drivers
steps.detail: Open GeForce Experience or Radeon Software and check for driver updates. Install any available updates.

steps.title: Check GPU Model
steps.detail: Open your system information or use software like GPU-Z to confirm your GPU model supports ray tracing.

steps.title: Enable Ray Tracing in Game
steps.detail: Access the game's settings menu, navigate to Graphics or Video settings, and enable ray tracing. Save changes and restart the game.

faqs.question: What games support ray tracing?
faqs.answer: Many modern games support ray tracing, including titles like 'Cyberpunk 2077', 'Control', and 'Minecraft'.

faqs.question: Can I run ray tracing on older GPUs?
faqs.answer: Older GPUs without dedicated ray tracing cores will not support ray tracing effectively, resulting in poor performance or inability to enable the feature.

faqs.question: Does ray tracing affect performance?
faqs.answer: Yes, enabling ray tracing can significantly impact performance, often requiring lower settings or resolution for smooth gameplay.

caveats: Performance may vary based on the specific hardware and game optimizations.
